items.title: NASA Science
items.summary: What color is the Moon? It depends on the night -- and the time. Outside of the Earth's atmosphere, the dark Moon, which shines by reflected sunlight, appears a magnificently brown-tinged gray. The featured image highlights a collection of apparent colors of the full moon on Earth, documented by one astrophotographer over 10 years from different locations across Italy. A red- or yellow-colored moon usually indicates a moon seen near the horizon. There, some of the blue light has been scattered away by a long path through the Earth's atmosphere, sometimes laden with fine dust. A blue-colored moon is more rare and can indicate an atmosphere carrying larger dust particles.

items.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
items.summary: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are an important source of systematic uncertainty in weak gravitational lensing measurements and also serve as a test for models of galaxy formation and evolution. These galaxy alignments are usually modeled assuming that the IA are sourced by the tidal fields around the galaxies. However, galaxy properties, like their proximity to other galaxies and their mass, provide alignment contributions beyond the tidal field. In this work, we perform novel model-agnostic tests to determine the impact of density-weighting on the IA of galaxies using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and SDSS-III (BOSS). We show that the primary effect of density-weighting is an increase of the alignment amplitude at large scales, whereas the small-scale impact is sample-dependent.
items.author: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek et al.

items.title: Secret-shared teleportation of a two-qudit gate with a deferred recipient
items.summary: An unknown quantum operation, like an unknown quantum state, cannot be perfectly copied or stored for later use. A specific gate can be embedded in an entangled resource and teleported, but its destination is fixed when the resource is created. Here we show that the capability to apply a two-qudit entangling gate can instead be secret-shared among many parties: the shares are distributed in advance, and a later key release lets exactly one of them, chosen after distribution, exercise it. A provider encrypts half of a Bell pair held with a user into $n$ shares, one per candidate node. The selected node, given the key qudits, completes an exact non-local $\mathtt{CSUM}^{k}$ gate with the user's data, in every measurement branch and for any qudit dimension, with the power $k$ chosen by the user alone.
items.author: Tanay Roy

items.title: A first look at strange-quark polarization in top-quark decays with CMS Open Data
items.summary: We present a first realization of strange-quark polarimetry in top-quark decays. The longitudinal polarization of $Λ$ baryons is measured in the strange jets of hadronic $W\to c\bar s$ decays in semileptonic top-quark pair events, using 16.39 fb$^{-1}$ of the public CMS data of pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. The $W$ decay produces the strange quark fully polarized, so that the $Λ$ polarization measures the transfer of the quark polarization in fragmentation. With the limited statistics available, our result is consistent both with zero and with the transfer inferred from the flavor-averaged LEP measurements. The statistical reach with the full Run-2, Run-3 and HL-LHC datasets is projected.
items.author: Yevgeny Kats

items.title: Time-optimal quantum dynamics under fixed-norm generators
items.summary: We investigate the dynamics of quantum systems whose evolution is governed by linear generators of fixed unitarily invariant norm. For this broad class of evolutions, we derive a universal time-optimal generator of the dynamics converting one given state into another. It provides a time-optimal non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for pure state conversion. We then use this general result to derive quantum speed limits for mixed-state evolutions governed by Lindbladians and non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. Our findings follow from the geometric properties of the group $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, in particular the geodesic distance. The derived bounds hold for an arbitrary system size $n$, depend only on the norms of the evolution generator and the initial and final states, and do not require performing any time-averaging.
items.author: Oskar A. Prośniak, Karol Życzkowski

items.title: Weighted hypergraph states as a resource for quantum metrology
items.summary: Quantum correlations can be used to improve sensing precision beyond classical limits, yet the correlated resource states needed can be challenging to prepare and preserve. Here, we study the family of weighted hypergraph states and identify subclasses characterized by their underlying graph topology that exhibit enhanced metrological performance. Using the quantum Fisher information and a novel Dicke state basis representation, we show that these subclasses outperform both separable and standard weighted graph state benchmarks over broad ranges of edge weights corresponding to weak controlled operations between qubits representing the vertices of the graph. We provide analytical formulas for an arbitrary number $N$ of qubits, supplemented by a general study, while focusing a detailed analysis on the example case of $N=4$.
items.author: B. J. Alexander, M. S. Tame

items.title: Persistence of Unitary Almost Mathieu Operator Gaps Ten Dry Martinis, Five on the Rim
items.summary: We determine exactly which gap labels are realized by open spectral gaps for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at every irrational frequency and all coupling constants ($0<λ_1,λ_2\leq1$). When both couplings are strictly less than one, every permitted gap label is realized by an open gap, including in the critical case ($λ_1=λ_2$). When at least one coupling equals one, both lifts of every odd winding label are realized by open gaps, whereas all even winding labels are collapsed. The proof combines quantitative almost reducibility and Aubry duality with a monotonicity principle for gap heights.
items.author: Dan S. Borgnia, Matthew Faust, Long Li

items.title: Functional Tensor Trains for High-Order Greeks and Exposure Tails of Multi-Asset Structured Products
items.summary: Risk management of worst-of autocallables needs price sensitivities (Greeks) up to third order and the potential future exposure, a tail quantile of the note's future value. In Monte Carlo, each order of differentiation multiplies the sampling noise by a factor that grows with the observation frequency, and nested simulation turns the noise of its inner paths into a bias of the quantile. We instead solve the backward pricing recursion, storing the continuation value as an $hp$ functional tensor train (hp-FTT) whose piecewise-polynomial cores are split at the barriers, so that worst-of barrier events act exactly, with rank one. For Gaussian transitions we show that the polynomial degree sufficient for an error $\varepsilon$ grows only as $\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}$.
items.author: Javier Lopez-Piqueres, Atithi Acharya, Yue Sun et al.

items.title: Topologically Protected Edge States in a Single Flux Qubit
items.summary: We show that topological edge states can be realized in a simple superconducting circuit composed of an inductively shunted flux qubit. The Josephson potential of that qubit forms a honeycomb lattice similar to the case of graphene. The additional shunting element produces a quartic potential along one flux direction, which effectively creates a boundary in flux space. We map analytically the low-energy dynamics of the circuit to an extended Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) chain, in which a quartic potential is added to the usual SSH Hamiltonian. This mapping is confirmed by numerical simulations of the full superconducting circuit. We argue that chiral symmetry still holds for the edge states of the extended model around a chiral point in parameter space.
items.author: Pablo Perez-Fernandez, Manuel Pino

items.title: Prognostic value of the preoperative C-reactive protein-to-lymphocyte ratio in patients with non-metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma
items.summary: by Minchao Qin, Zhongwen Feng, Chao Zhang, Wei Song, Kai Wang, Zhen Chen Background Systemic inflammation is associated with the prognosis of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). The C-reactive protein-to-lymphocyte ratio (CLR) combines systemic inflammation and host immune status. However, its prognostic value in non-metastatic ccRCC remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between preoperative CLR and survival outcomes in patients with non-metastatic ccRCC. Methods We retrospectively included 414 patients with non-metastatic ccRCC who underwent partial or radical nephrectomy. The primary Cox analyses treated ln(CLR) as a continuous variable and assessed overall survival (OS) and the cause-specific hazard of ccRCC-related death.
items.author: Minchao Qin, Zhongwen Feng, Chao Zhang et al.

items.title: Development of a competency framework for public health nurses in China: A modified Delphi study
items.summary: by Chunxia He, Lingli Yan, Jia Yin, Qian Yao, Jiali Zhang, Jimei Zhang, Xiuying Hu Background Public health nurses play a pivotal role in primary public health services, yet China lacks a systematic, context-specific competency framework to support workforce development. This study aimed to develop a competency framework for public health nurses in China to guide capacity-building initiatives. Methods A preliminary competency framework was constructed based on a literature review, job analysis, and semi-structured interviews with 22 frontline practitioners and comprised six domains, 16 subdomains, and 52 competencies. A two-round Delphi survey was then conducted with 21 experts from multiple regions with expertise in community nursing, public health, primary care medicine, and nursing education and related specialties.

items.title: Detection of potentially curable recurrence after colorectal cancer surgery in a real-world population
items.summary: by Ivonne J. H. Schoenaker, Richard M. Brohet, Evelyn J. Finnema, Dominique C. Damminga, Helle-Brit Fiebrich, Wouter H. de Vos tot Nederveen Cappel, Henderik L. van Westreenen Introduction After curative surgery for colorectal cancer (CRC), patients undergo surveillance because of the risk of recurrence; however, only a subset develops recurrence amenable to further curative-intent treatment. The primary aim of follow‑up is to identify patients with potentially curable recurrence. Materials and methods A retrospective analysis was performed of stage I–IV CRC patients who underwent curative-intent treatment and entered postoperative surveillance at Isala between 2014 and 2018. Follow‑up was conducted according to Dutch guideline‑based protocols for 60 months.

items.title: Age-specific income losses due to HPV-attributable cancers in Singapore
items.summary: by Robin Blythe, Nicholas Graves, N. Gopalakrishna Iyer, Marco A. Peres Introduction The link between Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cancer is well-established. In Singapore, bivalent HPV vaccines are subsidised for females, but not males. Economic analysis of HPV vaccination has generally assessed the costs to the health system, but this may not be as relevant to individual decision-making as potential lost income. We estimated the impact of bivalent HPV 16/18 vaccination on sick leave, unemployment, and premature mortality as a function of age and sex to understand the broader impact of HPV-related cancers. Methods We developed a population-level economic model to estimate lifetime income losses by diagnosis age, sex and cancer type.

items.title: Electronic health record phenotype choice and real-world outcome estimates: A propensity score–matched comparison of three invasive breast cancer definitions in TriNetX
items.summary: by Jui-Kun Chiang, Po-Chen Chiang, Malcolm Koo Electronic health record-based oncology studies depend on computable case definitions, but different operational definitions may identify different patient populations and change downstream estimates. This retrospective benchmarking cohort study evaluated three definitions of incident invasive breast cancer in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network: at least one malignant breast cancer diagnosis code (Dx1), a repeated diagnosis-code definition within 90 days (Dx2), and a diagnosis code plus breast cancer-directed treatment evidence (DxTx). Female patients aged 20 years or older were identified after a 12-month washout period and exclusion of patients with carcinoma in situ only. Pairwise one-to-one propensity-score matching was performed using 13 baseline covariates.

items.title: Hudson River Estuary sediments contain high fractional abundances of preserved globothalamean foraminiferal organic linings at Piermont, New York
items.summary: by Logan Brenner, Laura Haynes, Batoul Saad, Maisie Klem, Amelia Lang, Elizabeth Grey Linsley, William Riley, Sophie Spink, Carolyn Zhao, Margie Turrin, Lorelei Curtin Foundational to an estuarine ecosystem is the composition of its sediments, with benthic foraminifera serving as a key component. While it is common to find intact and deformed tests, foraminiferal organic linings (FOLs; foraminifera whose tests dissolved) are not always present in sediment samples. Identifying where FOLs are preserved is a necessary first step towards determining what promotes their development and burial. Here we document the prevalence of globothalamean FOLs in the Hudson River Estuary (HRE) at the Pier in Piermont, New York, USA.

items.title: MHC-II deficiency in a large Algerian cohort: Clinical, immunological, and genetic characterization.
items.summary: MHC class II (MHC-II) deficiency is a rare inborn error of immunity caused by defects in transcriptional regulators of MHC-II expression. In this study, we characterized the clinical, immunological, and molecular features of 107 patients from 98 unrelated Algerian families. Median ages at symptom onset and diagnosis were 5 and 14 mo, respectively, with pneumonia (82%) and chronic diarrhea (73%) predominating. CD4+ T cell lymphopenia occurred in 87.6% and naïve CD4+ T cell depletion in 86.0%. Among 99 genetically characterized patients, variants were identified exclusively in RFXANK (77.8%) and RFXAP (22.2%), including two predominant mutations (RFXANK c.338-25_338del and RFXAP c.368del) and four novel variants.

items.title: Combined Nav1.7-Nav1.8 channel abrogation: Supralinear suppression of excitability in a subpopulation of peripheral sensory neurons.
items.summary: There is a pressing need for nonaddictive pain therapeutics. Despite the genetic validation of peripheral voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels as targets for non-opioid pain therapy, isoform-selective inhibition of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 has yielded limited efficacy in clinical studies, with Nav1.8 blockade providing statistically significant but only partial pain relief. This raises the question: if block of Nav1.8 relieves pain only partially, what is needed for better pain relief? In this study, we utilized dynamic clamp, which permits precisely calibrated functional addition or subtraction of the current from any given channel, to systematically interrogate the combinatorial landscape of multiplex abrogation of currents from Nav1.7 and Nav1.8, both major contributors to electrogenesis within dorsal root ganglion neurons.

items.title: Nanobiomechanics in Oncology: Atomic Force Microscopy for Cancer Mechanophenotyping Using Cellular Young's Modulus.
items.summary: This review examines the current literature on the application of atomic force microscopy (AFM) to cancer mechanophenotyping, with particular emphasis on cellular Young's modulus and its potential diagnostic significance. A structured electronic search of PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar was conducted to identify studies published between 1999 and 2025 reporting AFM-based measurements of cellular Young's modulus in cancer-related models. Across multiple malignancies, reduced cellular stiffness is frequently observed in malignant compared with non-malignant cells and is associated with cytoskeletal remodelling, increased deformability and altered cell-matrix interactions. However, the relationship between Young's modulus and malignancy is not universally monotonic. Nanomechanical properties may vary across different pathological states and malignant phenotypes rather than following a simple monotonic trajectory, while invasive and metastatic cells can dynamically remodel their cytoskeleton and modify their stiffness in response to environmental and mechanical constraints.

items.title: Epstein-Barr Virus Serologic Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease.
items.summary: Background and objectives Although the link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and multiple sclerosis (MS) is well established, geographic variation in EBV epidemiology warrants region-specific data from Asian populations. Beyond MS, the role of EBV in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) remains far less studied. This study aimed to compare EBV serostatus and antibody titers in patients with MS, MOGAD, and controls in a Korean cohort. Methods We analyzed MS (n = 130), MOGAD (n = 125), and untreated tumor controls without known EBV association (n = 132). MS and controls were frequency-matched to MOGAD by age at sampling. Serum Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) IgG, viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgG, VCA IgM, and early antigen (EA) IgG were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassays (LIAISON, DiaSorin).
